newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, market seen aimless.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, market seen aimless.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.38 percent on Friday on low turnover amid a lack of trading incentives and traders forecast the market would continue trading with little clear direction.

"The market is desperate for some information concerning future of foreign investments. Turnover will stay on similar levels until fresh information about the issue becomes available," one trader said.

The central bank last month blocked the inflow of foreign investment by ordering international portfolio investors to open special custody accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licensed banks in order to trade in Slovenian securities.
Banks said the cost of opening an account would be about 12 percent of the amount handled. Banks said they planned to open the first accounts by the end of March.
The SBI index fell 5.35 points to 1,390.99, ending a five-day rising streak. This week the index firmed 0.96 percent.
"On such low turnover even the smallest move on the market can move the index in any direction," the trader said.
Overall six shares fell, eight rose and three were unchanged, while nine were untraded. Turnover fell to 53.9 million tolars from 54.1 million.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 1.70 percent to 55,050 tolars on volume of 402 shares for total turnover of 22.2 million tolars.
Bank UBK was the leading decliner, tumbling 10 percent to 5,850 tolars on volume of 112 shares.
Brokerage Dadas was the biggest gainer, jumping 11.53 percent to 8,030 tolars on volume of 400 shares for total turnover of 7.2 million tolars. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
